head:
Executive Orde
Under and pursuant to the provisions of section 18, paragraph (k), of the act
of Congress approved May 24, 1924, entitled "An Act For the reorganization and
improvement of the Foreign Service of the United States, and for other purposes ",
which paragraph reads as follows:
"(k) The President is authorized from time to time to establish,
.w~ ~ by Executive order, a list of places in tropical countries which by
reason of climatic or other extreme conditions are to be classed as
unhealthful posts, and each year of duty at such posts, while so classed,
inclusive of regular leaves of absence, shall be counted as one year
and a half, and so on in like proportion in reckoning the length of
service for the purposes of retirement"
the following place is hereby established as an unhealthful post for the purposes of
retirement within the meaning of the law above quoted, in addition to those places'
listed in Executive Order No. 4187 of April 1, 1925:
Tananarive, Madaascar.

head:
Executive 0rber
Mrs. Mary Hazard Teele may be appointed to a clerical position in the
Department of Agriculture without examination under the civil service rules.
Mrs. Teele is the widow of Mr. Ray P. Teele, Agricultural Economist, who
was employed in the Department of Agriculture almost continuously since 1899.
Mr. Teele died suddenly August 31, 1927, while on a special field assignment to the
Interior Department in connection with an investigation of reclamation projects in
Indian Reservations. Mrs. Teele has no adequate means of support and the Sec-
retary of Agriculture recommends her appointment.
The Civil Service Commission is unable to concur.
Done for charity.
CALVIN COOLIDGE
THE WHITE HOUSE,
November 28, 1927.
